title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
layout_note: Left panel: role agents placed around a central shared message store (two above, two below, one at the right), each joined to it by a blue double-headed arrow, with publish/subscribe tabs on the store's right edge and a tools legend under the panel. Right panel: a zoom into one role, joined to its avatar on the left by thin curved black lines: a profile card on top, then a memory strip and an iterative code-execute-debug loop below.
grouping: Each panel is a large rounded rectangle; the right one has a light blue-grey fill with white inner cards. The shared message store is a lavender rounded panel with a dashed outline and a bold serif title; inside it, individual messages are grey tag chips (msgA–msgD) bracketed to one expanded message showing its structured fields as key: value lines. A dotted rectangle encloses the programming loop in the zoom panel. Tools are listed in a separate legend box under the left panel, each with its icon.
shapes_depth: Flat. Agents are round cartoon avatar portraits on blue discs with the role name in bold serif below and a tool icon plus name beside it. Memory is a horizontal segmented strip (a tape of cells, one highlighted). The generated code is a syntax-coloured listing; the document being written is a yellow sticky note with a folded corner. Thin dotted arrows carry messages between agents, bold blue arrows join agents to the store, thin black arrows run the programming loop, whose two exits are marked by a red cross (to Debug) and a green check (Add Code). An ear icon marks subscription.
proposed_highlight: The shared message pool is the hub everyone connects to and the only lavender region; the per-agent mechanism is shown in an enlarged detail panel on the right with its own memory strip and feedback loop.
lesson: For a team of role agents, place avatar portraits around a central shared store linked by double-headed arrows, show one message expanded as key: value fields, and pull one agent out into a side panel that zooms into its profile, memory and execute-feedback loop.
notes: elements 'other' = the memory tape strip, the sticky-note document and the check/cross outcome glyphs. Venue and year from the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024').

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: multi-agent software development with shared message pool

core.what: five role avatars placed around one central purple Shared Message Pool, each tied to it by a vertical blue double arrow, with one expanded message shown as key-value fields inside the pool

relations.form: the purple pool sits in the middle of the left frame; Architect and Project Manager above, Product Manager and QA Engineer below, and the Engineer at the right connect through 'subscription' and 'publish' boxes on the pool's right edge
dotted arrows around the outside of the left frame chain the roles Architect to Project Manager to Engineer to QA Engineer to Product Manager
a curved black line leaves the Engineer and opens a large blue rounded panel on the right holding an 'Agent Profile' card (Name, Profile, Goal, Constraint) and the engineer's working loop

inside the zoom panel a dotted 'Iterative Programming' frame draws a loop: a code snippet produced from 'Write game.py' goes to Execution, a red cross returns through Debug and a 'Feedback' line to the LLM icon, a green check sends 'Add Code' up to History Message
a Memory tape strip at the top of the work area is read by 'Memory Retrieval' into a History Message box listing PRD Document, System Design and Code

channels.colour: purple = the shared pool and also the History Message header; blue double arrows = publish/subscribe; red cross / green check = execution failed / passed; tool icons coloured by tool (keyed in a Tools legend at the bottom)
channels.shape: cartoon avatars = agents; grey 'msg' tabs = messages; key-value text = one message's fields; a code listing = real output
channels.line: solid blue double arrows = pool traffic; dotted arrows = role-to-role order; curved black lines = zoom from the Engineer
channels.frame: black rounded frame = the agent team; blue rounded panel = one agent opened up; dotted frame = the iterative-programming loop

quality.strengths: the shared pool is literally central with every agent wired to it, and one message is expanded as its real fields (content, cause_by, sent_from, send_to); the zoom panel shows the agent's work as real code and an execution/debug loop
quality.weaknesses: the zoom panel is larger than the team overview and densely packed, so the eye goes to the code listing rather than the pool; the dotted role-order arrows run around the frame edge and are easy to miss; purple marks both the pool and History Message; a second curved line from the panel's bottom back to 'publish' crosses the gap with no label

insights.structure: Left: a rounded frame with five role avatars (Architect, Project Manager, Engineer, Product Manager, QA Engineer) placed around a central purple 'Shared Message Pool'; right: a large blue zoom panel pulled out of the Engineer, holding an 'Agent Profile' card on top and an 'Iterative Programming' loop below.
insights.data: Agents are cartoon avatar portraits with tool icons, one message is expanded as key: value fields (content, cause_by, sent_from, send_to), and the engineer's work is shown as a real code snippet next to a sticky note and a memory tape strip.
insights.emphasis: The shared message pool is the central tinted block with double-headed blue arrows to every agent, and a curved black line zooms from the Engineer into the right-hand panel.
insights.flow: Agents publish to and subscribe from the pool by vertical double arrows; dotted arrows trace the hand-off order around the perimeter; in the right panel the loop runs write code, execution, check/cross, then Debug or Add Code back around.
insights.avoid: Too many small icons (pdf, python, image, document glyphs floating near agents) and two separate loops of dotted arrows make the left panel busy, and the 'Tools' legend sits detached below.

arrangement.units: a rounded frame for the agent team around a shared pool on the left, and a larger blue rounded zoom panel for one agent on the right with nested white cards
arrangement.inputs_as: agent profile text and structured messages
arrangement.shared: the shared message pool, drawn once at the centre of the left panel
